### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

Desktop canary users on `v2.3.2-canary.1` can't update: **Check for updates** says they're on the latest version, although `v2.3.2-canary.2` is on GitHub Releases. They also stopped receiving core OTA updates.

Cause: in [run 41944676897](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/actions/runs/41944676897), R2 rejected the arm64 dmg upload with `InvalidPart` on `CompleteMultipartUpload`. The same runner image, CLI and script uploaded canary.1 two days earlier, and no other job was writing that key, so this looks transient. The core OTA and `canary/shell.json` for the new shell had already gone up before that failure. As a result:

- The installer manifests and the Sparkle appcast never shipped. They still list canary.1.
- Later core-only runs published 18 cores under `2.3.2-canary.2`, a shell no client could install.
- Re-running the job could not repair this, because the core seq guard rejects republishing r0 behind seq 18.

**Upload failure.** Changes to `desktop-publish-s3`:

- **Retry:** retry each installer and manifest upload as a whole file, up to 3 attempts with 15s and 30s backoff. A retry starts a fresh multipart upload. `aws s3 cp` only retries individual requests, never a rejected multipart completion.
- **Reorder:** the old single upload step is split in two:
  - **Upload installers** runs before the core and `shell.json`. If it fails, nothing is visible yet, later core-only runs keep targeting the previous shell, and the job can simply be re-run.
  - **Publish installer manifests** runs after the core, so the manifests clients poll appear only once their installers and the new shell's core exist.
- **Outputs and diagnostics:** `installers-published` now comes from the manifests step. The release diagnostics classify a manifest failure as `installer-manifest-upload-failed`.

**Manual full release never built.** A `workflow_dispatch` with `force_full: true` skips `core-ota`. GitHub Actions skips every job whose ancestor was skipped unless the job sets its own `if:`. So `calculate-version` succeeded (it computed `2.3.2-canary.3`), and then lint, build, upload and publish were all skipped ([run 42005206388](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/actions/runs/42005206388)). The `!inputs.force_full` gate came in with #19501. Since then, the only way to cut a full canary release has been a push whose shell ABI changed.

- Every job after `calculate-version` now states `!cancelled()` plus success of its direct dependencies. The push path keeps its previous behavior: any failed or skipped dependency still stops the jobs after it.
- New `.github/scripts/release-desktop-canary.test.mjs` walks every job downstream of `core-ota` and fails if one falls back to the default `success()` condition. It fails against the previous workflow.

#### Key Decisions / Non-goals

- The retry covers only this action's installer and manifest uploads. The shared `desktop-publish-core-ota` uploads are unchanged.
- This does not repair the already-broken canary.2 state. A new full canary build replaces it.

#### Test

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added/updated tests
- `release-desktop-canary.test.mjs` (see above); both node tests run in the `Test Packages` job.

- New `.github/scripts/desktop-publish-s3.test.mjs`, wired into the `Test Packages` job. It runs the action's real installer script against a fake `aws` that fails like R2: two failures followed by a success uploads the file, and three failures fail the step after three attempts. It also asserts the step order installers → core → manifests. Both tests fail against the previous action.
- `reportRendererOta.test.mjs` covers the new diagnostic stage.
- Acceptance: Not needed: release CI tooling only, no product behavior change. The next full desktop release exercises it.


🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits.messageBody:
…ore OTA

R2 rejected the v2.3.2-canary.2 arm64 dmg with InvalidPart on
CompleteMultipartUpload after the core OTA and shell.json for the new shell
were already live, so the installer manifests and Sparkle appcast never
shipped while later core-only runs published cores no client could reach.

- Retry each installer and manifest upload as a whole file (3 attempts).
- Upload installers before the core/shell.json and the manifests after it,
  so a failed installer upload leaves nothing half-published.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

…publish jobs

force_full skips core-ota, and a skipped ancestor skips every job left on the
default success() condition, so a manual full release computed its version and
then skipped lint, build, upload and publish. Each job after calculate-version
now checks its direct dependencies explicitly.

### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

When a server-side agent run is routed to the caller's own desktop, `executionPlanToManifestExecutionEnv` maps the plan to manifest `executionEnv: 'local'` (kept distinct so `lobe-local-system` can return images). `resolveSkillsManifest` only treated `'device'` as a routed device, so for `'local'` it returned the static manifest: the model was offered the sandbox-only `lobe-skills` `runCommand` / `exportFile`, and the skills systemRole told it to `exportFile` every artifact.

The server skills runtime receives the same `activeDeviceId` and refuses both APIs ("runCommand targets the cloud sandbox and is unavailable while a local device is routed…"). Observed in a production topic: the model put an entire generated HTML file into `lobe-skills.runCommand`, got refused, and then had to regenerate the whole output through another tool — one extra very long generation that ended in an upstream gateway timeout.

This PR treats `'local'` like `'device'` in `resolveSkillsManifest`: `runCommand` / `exportFile` are hidden, `execScript` gets the device execution preamble, and the tool systemRole gets the `<execution_environment>` block pointing at `lobe-local-system` runCommand. Remote devices (`deviceId !== localDeviceId`) already mapped to `'device'` and are unchanged. Electron client-side runs resolve `manifest.desktop.ts`, which only exposes `execScript`, so their API set is unchanged.

#### Test

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] No tests needed

- `resolveManifest.test.ts`: `'local'` now goes through the same device assertions as `'device'` (failed before the fix, passes after). `bun run check` on the changed files: lint clean, 18 tests passed; related `execAgent.deviceToolPipeline`, `streamingExecutor` and skills package tests: 75 passed; full type-check: no errors.
- Acceptance: https://lobehub.com/acceptance/8138c854-5877-4a82-9571-8be35e0157ac — before/after server runs on a local device-gateway closed loop (caller desktop routed, remote-device control), with captured model tool lists and the rendered tool cards

#### 🔗 Related Issue

None found.

commits.messageBody:
…esktop is routed

When the run is routed to the caller's own desktop, the execution plan maps to
manifest executionEnv `local` (kept distinct so local-system can return images),
but resolveSkillsManifest only hid the sandbox-only APIs for `device`, so `local`
fell back to the static manifest. The server skills runtime still receives the
routed activeDeviceId and refuses runCommand / exportFile, so the model was told
to use APIs that always fail — and to exportFile every artifact — then had to
regenerate its whole output through another tool.

Treat `local` like `device`: drop runCommand / exportFile and declare device
execution on execScript. Electron client-side runs use manifest.desktop.ts,
which already exposes only execScript, so their API set is unchanged.

### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

The Linear import scope in a project could only be a whole team or one Linear project. A team that had already imported its project issues had no way to pick out, or keep syncing, the issues that belong to no Linear project. "All projects" mixes them with every project issue not yet imported, and the picker cannot filter down to them.

This PR adds a **No project / 无项目** scope:

- **Import dialog, step 1:** the "Linear project" select gets a `No project` option, and the hint explains it.
- **Server:** `toIssueFilter` sends `{ team, project: { null: true }, state }` for this scope. Linear's `IssueFilter.project` is a `NullableProjectFilter` with `null: Boolean`.
- **Sync closing pass:** for this scope it runs over the team, like a whole-team rule, and skips the project-teams lookup. An issue that later moves into a project and closes there still gets its task closed.
- **Saved rules:** they work as before. The rule list and sync job titles read `Engineering › No project`.

#### Key Decisions / Non-goals

- **No schema change.** The scope is stored as the sentinel `LINEAR_NO_PROJECT_ID = 'none'` in the existing nullable `linear_sync_rules.linear_project_id` column. Linear project ids are UUIDs, so it cannot collide. `linear_project_name` is stored as null for it, and the client renders the localized label.
- **Rollback note:** if this is reverted after users save No-project rules, older code would treat `'none'` as a project id. Those rules would then match nothing or fail with a Linear error until they are deleted. No data is lost.
- **Locales:** en-US and zh-CN are hand-written. Other locales are left to the daily auto-i18n workflow, because `bun run i18n` could not run here (no translation key).

#### Test

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added/updated tests
  - `issues.test.ts`: the No-project filter shape.
  - `issueSync.integration.test.ts` (real PG): syncs no-project issues, and never looks up `'none'` as a project.
  - Router test: a No-project rule is saved with a null name and runs with the sentinel.
  - `utils.test.ts`: the scope label.
- `bun run check --lint --test --type`: clean, 96 tests passed.

- Acceptance: https://app.lobehub.com/acceptance/0300cc5e-e6cc-4280-8be0-e5406b5ba849
  - Local dev, Web UI, against an in-process fake Linear that applies the received filters and logs them. Real Linear was not exercised.
  - Round 2 re-publishes round 1's evidence, because round 1's evidence upload was rejected by token scope.

#### 🔗 Related Issue

Related to LobeHub task T-6156.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits.messageBody:
The import scope could only be a whole team or one Linear project, so
issues without a project could not be picked or synced on their own into
a LobeHub project. Add a "No project" scope (stored as the
LINEAR_NO_PROJECT_ID sentinel in the existing linear_project_id column,
no schema change) that filters the team's issues with project null, and
label it in the scope summary, rule list and sync job titles.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

The bulk actions panel ("Assign to agent…" after multi-selecting tasks) had two problems:

1. **No grouping.** It listed every agent flat from `allAgents`. The single-task assignee picker groups them like the sidebar (private / workspace scope → pinned → sidebar groups → default list, plus inbox and "Recently assigned").
2. **Private agents silently skipped public tasks.** Picking a private agent sent `batchUpdate` straight away, and the server skipped every public task as `invalid` (the task-visibility invariant). The single-task picker instead asks first, makes the task private (taking it over when someone else created it) and then assigns it.

Changes:

- Extract `useAssigneeAgentScopes` (scopes, sections, inbox, private agent ids, recent bookkeeping) from `AssigneeAgentSelector` and use it in both pickers so they group agents the same way. The bulk panel renders each section as a cmdk group; since cmdk groups don't nest, a section heading names its scope too (`Private · Pinned`, `Workspace · <group>`). Recent hides while searching, as in the single picker.
- Picking a private agent when the selection holds public tasks now opens a confirmation (the same `VisibilityConfirmContent` as the single picker, the number of tasks that go private, and a warning with the count of teammates' tasks that get taken over). On confirm, the public non-running tasks go private through the existing `updateVisibility` endpoint (with `takeOwnership` for teammates' tasks, 5 at a time; failures are left public and reported as skipped by the batch). The whole selection is then assigned in one batch. Cancelling changes nothing.
- `useTaskBatchActions.run` takes an optional `prepare` step that runs in the request queue after the optimistic overlay and before the batch request.
- Fix a lobe-design lint FAIL in the single picker's search box (`outline: none` without an alternative focus indicator).

No server or database changes. Undo of the batch reverts the assignee only, not the visibility change, which matches the single-task picker.

| Before | After |
| ------ | ----- |
| Flat agent list (see acceptance, check 1) | Grouped like the sidebar: inbox, Recently assigned, Pinned, sidebar groups, Default List (see acceptance, check 1) |

#### Test

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added/updated tests

Unit tests: `TaskBulkActionsPanel.test.tsx` (grouping, workspace agent assigns directly, private agent confirms first, then privatizes and assigns; fails on the old panel), `privatizeTasks.test.ts`, `pickTasksToPrivatize`, and the `prepare` ordering in `useTaskBatchActions.test.ts`. All 56 selection tests pass. `type-check` and the lobe-design lint (0 FAIL) pass.

- Acceptance: https://lobehub.com/lobehub/acceptance/db395305-977e-4b02-aeb6-844a9d1fdc17 (4/4 passed). Round 1 ran on the OSS local web app and covered grouping (before/after), direct assignment of a workspace agent, and the single-picker regression. Round 2 ran in a local Cloud workspace with the same changes. It covered the Private / Workspace groups and the private-agent confirmation (3 public tasks, 1 of them a teammate's). Cancel left every task untouched and kept the agent out of Recent. Confirm made the tasks private and assigned all 4 ("4 tasks updated", none skipped).

#### 🔗 Related Issue

Internal task T-5080.

commits.messageBody:
…nfirm before assigning a private agent (T-5080)

The bulk actions panel listed every agent flat and sent a private agent
straight to batchUpdate, where every public task was skipped as invalid.
It now shares useAssigneeAgentScopes with AssigneeAgentSelector (private /
workspace scopes, pinned, sidebar groups, recent, inbox), and picking a
private agent asks first, makes the public tasks private (taking over
teammates' tasks) and then assigns the whole selection.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

🐛 fix(task): record a bulk private-agent pick in Recent only after it…

### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

Clicking a GitHub PR Work card in chat used to always open GitHub in a new tab, even though the Working Sidebar already has a PR tab for that PR with live state, checks and merge. The card now opens that tab when the sidebar shows the same PR.

- The Working Sidebar's PR tab, now extracted to `PullRequest/SidebarTab.tsx`, publishes its PR URL to a session-only global store field (`workingSidebarPullRequestUrl`, outside persisted `status`). The tab stays mounted while the panel is collapsed. It publishes only while the panel has room for the tab (`widthBudget >= MIN_PANEL_WIDTH`) and clears the URL on unmount.
- `openExternalWork` compares the card URL with the published URL as `owner/repo#n`. The comparison ignores case, sub-pages, query and fragment. On a match it calls `openWorkingSidebar('pr')`.
- These cases still open GitHub: a different PR, no linked PR (for example, cloud sandbox runs), no room for the sidebar beside an open portal, and surfaces without the sidebar (mobile, project dashboard, shared pages, which pass their own `onOpen`). The http(s) allowlist is unchanged.
- Fix: the card's branch label had no font size, so it rendered at the inherited 14px next to the 12px `owner/repo#n` identifier. It now uses 12px, matching the identifier.

#### Test

- [ ] Tested locally
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] No tests needed

`bun run check --lint --test --type` passes.

New tests:
- `openExternalWork.test.ts` covers PR URL matching, opening the PR tab on a match, falling back to the URL otherwise, and refusing non-http(s) URLs.
- `usePublishPrUrl.test.ts` covers setting the published URL, clearing it when the tab cannot show, and clearing it on unmount.

- Acceptance: pending. The author will verify on the real product (a PR card in a GitHub working directory topic, clicked with the sidebar's PR tab present and absent) and add the acceptance link here.

#### 🔗 Related Issue

None.

### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

In a Channel, `@` used to suggest only members already in the Channel. Now, when someone who can invite types a name, the menu also lists matching **workspace members and Agents outside the Channel** under "Not in this channel · mention to add". Choosing one adds them to the Channel, the same as the Invite members dialog, and the message @mentions them as members.

- **Who sees outsiders:** only Channel admins (`canInviteMembers`) in a group Channel. Never in archived Channels or direct Agent conversations, which stay one person and one Agent. Personal Channels offer only Agents, because people join only workspace Channels.
- **When:** only after a name is typed; a bare `@` behaves as before. At most 5 people and 5 Agents, with the project's own Agents first.
- **Joining:** choosing an outsider adds them right away through the existing `addUser` / `addAgent` endpoints (new store action `channelActions.addMember` returns the member id). Agents take the invite dialog's inherited device/directory defaults, resolved by the same `useChannelAgentDraft` logic in a hidden component. An Agent the dialog could not add (for example its device is offline) fails here too.
- **Sending:** the composer waits for invites still in flight, retries failed ones, and turns invite chips into member mentions. If someone cannot join, an inline error names them and the draft stays unsent. Where inviting is unavailable (for example a chip pasted into a direct conversation), the chip stays plain text, like any chip for a non-member.
- **People search:** debounced like the invite dialog, because each `userCandidates` call takes the Channel lock on the server.
- Small refactor: `channelAgentIssueKey` moves into `agentEnvironment.ts` and is shared by `EnvironmentFields`.
- New en-US / zh-CN keys `channel:mentionInvite.*`.

No server or database changes.

#### Test

- [ ] Tested locally

`useMentionInvites.test.ts` covers candidate gating, debounced search, filtering out people who already joined, deduplicated invites, Agent environment defaults, blocked and timed-out Agents, failure with retry, and chips where inviting is disabled. `mentions.test.ts` and `mentionGroups.test.ts` cover chip parsing and Agent matching, and `action.test.ts` covers `addMember`. body:
### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

A single page-editor paste with many external images could freeze a whole server instance for the full function timeout (300s), failing every request routed to it.

**Mechanism.** The editor rehosts every pasted image at once, and tRPC batches them into one request. Each `file.rehostImage` → `uploadFromBuffer` opens a transaction that checks out a pool connection and waits on the owner's storage row lock. The transaction holding the lock then calls `fileModel.checkHash` **outside** the transaction, which needs an 11th connection from the default 10-connection pool. Every connection is held by a lock waiter, so nothing can progress. The pool has no acquire timeout, so every other query on the instance queues behind it until the platform kills the function. In production one batch of 78 rehosts failed about 200 unrelated requests on the same instance.

**Changes**

- `FileService.createFileRecord` runs `checkHash` and `updateGlobalFile` on the caller's `trx`. `FileModel.checkHash` accepts an optional `trx`.
- DB pools (node and neon drivers) get `connectionTimeoutMillis`, a new `DATABASE_POOL_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` setting that defaults to 30s (`0` keeps the old wait-forever behaviour). An exhausted pool now fails the requests that cannot get a connection instead of hanging the instance.
- The editor keeps at most 3 image rehosts in flight (`MAX_CONCURRENT_REHOSTS`).

The companion cloud change (storage lock `FOR UPDATE` → `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, so that lock no longer blocks the user's FK inserts) is in the cloud repo.

#### Test

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] No tests needed

- `apps/server/src/services/file/__tests__/index.test.ts`: new test checks that `uploadFromBuffer` runs `checkHash`, `updateGlobalFile` and `create` on the record transaction. It fails without the fix.
- `packages/database/src/core/web-server.test.ts`: tests the default acquire timeout, the override, and that statement timeouts are kept.
- `src/features/EditorCanvas/rehostImage.test.ts`: 20 parallel rehosts peak at 3 in flight, and a failed rehost releases its slot. Fails without the fix.
- `bun run check --lint` clean, `bun run check --type` clean.

- Acceptance: Not needed: no visible behavior change for a normal paste (images still rehost; only fewer run at once). The fixed failure is a pool deadlock under load, which the regression tests above reproduce at unit level. A browser run would not show it reliably.

#### 🔗 Related Issue

Production incident 2026-11-02 (one instance frozen 300s, about 200 requests failed with `FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED`).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits.messageBody:
On 2026-11-02 a page-editor paste sent 78 `file.rehostImage` calls in one
tRPC batch. Each `uploadFromBuffer` transaction checked out a pool
connection and waited on the owner's storage row lock; the lock holder then
called `fileModel.checkHash` outside its transaction and waited for an 11th
connection on the default 10-connection pool. Nothing could progress, and
every request on that Vercel instance queued behind the pool until the
function was killed at 300s (~200 requests failed with
FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED).

- createFileRecord runs checkHash / updateGlobalFile on the caller's trx
- pools get a 30s acquire timeout (DATABASE_POOL_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT, 0 = none)
  so an exhausted pool fails requests instead of hanging the instance
- the editor rehosts at most 3 images at a time
